subject: physics

sections.title: Introduction to the Physics of Hearing
learning_objectives: Define sound and hearing.

sections.title: Sound
learning_objectives: Define sound and hearing.
Describe sound as a longitudinal wave.

sections.title: Speed of Sound, Frequency, and Wavelength
learning_objectives: Define pitch.
Describe the relationship between the speed of sound, its frequency, and its wavelength.
Describe the effects on the speed of sound as it travels through various media.
Describe the effects of temperature on the speed of sound.

sections.title: Sound Intensity and Sound Level
learning_objectives: Define intensity, sound intensity, and sound pressure level.
Calculate sound intensity levels in decibels (dB).

sections.title: Doppler Effect and Sonic Booms
learning_objectives: Define Doppler effect, Doppler shift, and sonic boom.
Calculate the frequency of a sound heard by someone observing Doppler shift.
Describe the sounds produced by objects moving faster than the speed of sound.

sections.title: Sound Interference and Resonance: Standing Waves in Air Columns
learning_objectives: Define antinode, node, fundamental, overtones, and harmonics.
Identify instances of sound interference in everyday situations.
Describe how sound interference occurring inside open and closed tubes changes the characteristics of the sound, and how this applies to sounds produced by musical instruments.
Calculate the length of a tube using sound wave measurements.

sections.title: Hearing
learning_objectives: Define hearing, pitch, loudness, timbre, note, tone, phon, ultrasound, and infrasound.
Compare loudness to frequency and intensity of a sound.
Identify structures of the inner ear and explain how they relate to sound perception.

sections.title: Ultrasound
learning_objectives: Define acoustic impedance and intensity reflection coefficient.
Describe medical and other uses of ultrasound technology.
Calculate acoustic impedance using density values and the speed of ultrasound.
Calculate the velocity of a moving object using Doppler-shifted ultrasound.

misconception.text: Sound is a transverse wave, like light.

correction.text: In sound the particles of the medium oscillate along the direction of travel, so the wave is longitudinal. Light is transverse, and the difference is what makes sound need a medium and light not.

signal.text: Our own question offers transverse as the answer.

misconception.text: The speed of sound in air is about $1500\,\text{m/s}$.

correction.text: In air at room temperature it is about $340\,\text{m/s}$. The figure near $1500\,\text{m/s}$ belongs to sound in water, and $3 \times 10^8\,\text{m/s}$ is the speed of light.
